policy.topic: IRA Part D redesign - OOP cap
policy.summary: Annual out-of-pocket cap $2,000 in 2025, indexed to $2,100 for 2026 (one secondary source cites $2,400 for 2027 - unverified). Max deductible $615 in 2026.
policy.implication_dee: Minor: few DEE patients in Part D (adults with LGS/Dravet on SSDI are the exception).
policy.implication_et: Major positive for patient affordability/persistency: caps beneficiary cost for a branded ET drug; Medicare Prescription Payment Plan smooths costs.

policy.summary: Replaced Coverage Gap Discount Program in 2025: manufacturer pays 10% in initial coverage phase and 20% in catastrophic phase on applicable brands (one agent guide says 20% initial - outlier). Specified small manufacturer phase-in: schedule not retrieved (background knowledge, unverified: 1% 2025, 2% 2026, 5% 2027, 8% 2028, 10% 2029 for initial phase; catastrophic reaching 20% by 2031) - and applies to drugs marketed as of Aug 2022, so a new launch likely would not qualify.
policy.implication_et: Structural GTN hit: for a ~$60-110K/yr drug nearly all spend is catastrophic => ~20% mandatory discount on Part D volume, plus plan rebates. Skyclarys/Nuplazid 2025 results show the effect.

policy.summary: Small molecules eligible for selection 7 years after approval, MFP effective at year 9; biologics 11/13. EPIC Act (H.R. 1492, reintroduced Mar 2025) would equalise; April 2025 executive order directs HHS to work with Congress - no statutory change found as of late 2026.
policy.implication_et: A small-molecule ET blockbuster (>$200M Medicare spend) faces MFP at ~year 9-10 post launch; model a price step-down then.

policy.topic: ORPHAN Cures Act (in 2025 reconciliation law, 'One Big Beautiful Bill')
policy.summary: Orphan exclusion from negotiation extended to drugs with one OR MORE orphan designations (all indications orphan); 7/11-year clock starts only when a non-orphan indication is approved. Applies from third negotiation round (selection by Feb 1 2026; prices effective 2028 - effective year not confirmed in snippet). KFF: costs several billion over a decade. Democrats have proposed repeal / $400M spend threshold.
policy.implication_dee: Positive: DEE asset can add further rare indications (e.g., SCN2A + SCN8A + other DEEs) without losing exclusion.
policy.implication_et: None unless ET drug is orphan (ET is not rare). If same molecule has DEE (orphan) and ET (non-orphan) indications, exclusion is lost and clock starts at the non-orphan approval.

policy.summary: $911B in Medicaid cuts over 10 yrs (CBO): work requirements (80 hrs/month, expansion adults, from 2027-01-01; -$326B; -5.2M adults by 2034), provider-tax freeze/phasedown (-$226B), more frequent redeterminations for expansion adults. Total uninsured +14.2M with ACA changes (KFF, check). Enrollment already falling: 79.4M (Dec 2024) -> 74.3M (Mar 2026).
policy.implication_dee: Children/disabled pathways not directly targeted, but state budget pressure => tighter PDL/PA, supplemental-rebate demands, churn risk; pediatric Medicaid+CHIP down to 35.6M.
policy.implication_et: Limited (duals); state budget pressure affects Medicaid secondary coverage.

policy.summary: Lapsed Dec 2024; reauthorised through Sept 2029 by Consolidated Appropriations Act 2026 (Mikaela Naylon Give Kids a Chance Act), signed 2026-02-03. Recent sales: Abeona $155M (Jun 2025); Jazz $200M (Jan 2026).
policy.implication_dee: DEE approvals with RPD designation can earn a PRV worth ~$150-200M (non-dilutive).

policy.summary: 2025 EO led to manufacturer agreements: all 17 targeted manufacturers signed by ~Apr 2026 (16 by Feb 2026 incl. commitments to launch new drugs at MFN parity); TrumpRx DTC site live ~Feb 5 2026; GENEROUS Medicaid model (voluntary, 2026-2030, MFN from 8 countries); GLOBE (Part B) reported final, effective 2026-11-30, PhRMA suit filed 2026-10-07; GUARD (Part D) final rule not published as of Oct 2026. Reported Sec. 232 pharma tariffs up to 100% from 2026-07-31 with relief for MFN signatories (single source). Sources conflict on dates - verify at CMS/Federal Register.
policy.implication_dee: Launch-sequencing: ex-US launch price now constrains US Medicaid net price for signatories; small biotechs not among the 17 but GENEROUS/launch-parity norms may spread.
policy.implication_et: GUARD (Part D) would be the relevant model if finalised; uncertain.

policy.summary: No UPL has taken effect yet. Colorado set first UPL (Enbrel, Oct 2025, eff. Jan 2027) - preliminarily enjoined 2026-07-01 on patent pre-emption. Maryland set UPLs for Jardiance (Apr 2026) and Ozempic (May 2026) at Medicare MFP, eff. Jan 2027. Washington and Minnesota have boards but no completed reviews; MN statute ties UPL to MFP. Orphan carve-outs: sources conflict (Health Affairs: none; RAAP: Washington exempts single-indication orphan drugs).
policy.implication_dee: Low near-term risk; high-cost orphan drugs are review-eligible in most PDAB states.
policy.implication_et: Moderate long-term risk for a high-volume ET brand in PDAB states once MFP exists.

policy.summary: From 2024-01-01 Medicaid rebates can exceed 100% of AMP.
policy.implication_dee: Penalises steep post-launch price increases in a Medicaid-heavy book: set launch price right, keep increases <= CPI-U.
